title: The Sea That Vanished

script.text: About [6|six] million years ago, the Mediterranean Sea almost disappeared.

script: Its gateways to the Atlantic, in what is now Spain and Morocco, closed.

script.text: Rivers couldn't keep up with the sun.

script: The sea may have lost [70%|seventy percent] of its water.

script.text: What remained were shrinking, salty lakes, like giant Dead Seas.

script: Salt piled up on the seabed, in places up to [3|three] kilometers thick.
Then, [5.33|five point three three] million years ago, the Atlantic broke back in at Gibraltar.
One model says the flood peaked at about [100|one hundred] million cubic meters per second.

script.text: Roughly [500|five hundred] Amazon Rivers at once.

script: Sea level may have risen more than [10|ten] meters a day.

script.text: Up to [90%|ninety percent] of the sea, refilled in under two years.

script: Today, a gap just [14|fourteen] kilometers wide is all that keeps it full.
